name: 220-bottom-placement-mirrors-the-land
why: The first case whose land is stated FOOTPRINT-LOCAL and placed by a component, which is the only way to ask whether the two sides place a back-mounted part the same way. U2 sits at (10,10) turned 90 on the BOTTOM. Placing local (1.0, 2.0): the flip negates local y to (1.0, -2.0); the KiCad clockwise turn in this y-down frame sends (x,y) to (y,-x) at 90, giving (-2.0, -1.0); translation lands the centre at (8.0, 9.0). Skipping the mirror puts it at (12.0, 9.0) and mirroring AFTER the turn puts it at (12.0, 11.0) - three distinct points, so the offset is off-axis on purpose. The land is 1.6 x 1.0 with no turn of its own, so its board angle is the placement's 90 and its copper spans x 7.5..8.5, y 8.2..9.8. The probe sits at (8.0, 9.7), 0.1 mm inside the far y edge; an uncomposed land angle of 0 would span y 8.5..9.5 instead and leave the probe 0.2 mm out, which its 0.125 mm cap cannot reach.
